newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity ends higher on Western outages.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity ends higher on Western outages.

text.p: NYMEX electricity prices rose Wednesday on news of unplanned outages at several Western nuclear power plants, industry sources said.

The 1,073 Diablo Canyon 2 nuclear power unit in Avila Beach on California's central coast was taken off line early Wednesday due to a problem in the feedwater system, with no restart date yet available.
Also, Southern California Edison Co's 1,070 MW San Onofre unit 2 and 1,080 MW unit 3 were expected to resume operation around July 15 and July 10, respectively, company officials said Wednesday.
San Onofre 2 was shut Sunday to replace its charge line check valves, and San Onofre 3 has been out of service since April 12 for refueling and maintenance.
In addition, capacity at the 1,221 MW Palo Verde 3 nuclear unit near Phoenix, Ariz., has been trimmed by 10 percent for repair work expected to take 24 hours.

The repair work is related to a water leak in a small pump within the unit's secondary system, a spokesman for Arizona Public Service Co said. Unit 3 was expected to be back to full power sometime Thursday morning, he noted.

Power futures reacted to the outages, with August Palo Verde ending up $1.11 at $34.65 following exchanges in a range of $34.00-35.50 per megawatt hour (MWh), while September closed 50 cents higher at $28.90 following trades in a range of $28.40-29.10 per MWh.

August California Oregon Border (COB) settled up 37 cents at $23.30 following exchanges in a range of $23.00-23.40, while September ended up 30 cents at $23.20 after trade in a range of $23.00-23.30 per MWh.
NYMEX said an estimated total of 344 COB and 641 PV contracts had traded.
August Henry Hub natural gas futures closed down 4.3 cents at $2.067 per million British thermal units.

Meteorologists called for a warming trend to begin later this week in the Pacific Northwest following recent cooler-than-normal weather. Meanwhile, forecasts called for temperatures in the Southwest to stay near to above normal through next week.
NYMEX markets will close early Thursday in advance of the July 4 Independence Day holiday with PV ending trade at 1255 EDT and COB ending trade at $1300 EDT.
